verdict: IFF's sales rose 4% to $1.94B and day-to-day operations earned $160M — but a $236M write-down on the Food Ingredients business it is selling pushed the continuing business to a $127M loss.

segments.name: Taste
segments.note: Flavors for food and drinks — grew in every region, led by a double-digit increase in Greater Asia.

segments.name: Scent
segments.note: Fragrances for perfumes, soaps and detergents — consumer fragrances grew high-single digits.

segments.name: Health & Biosciences
segments.note: Enzymes, cultures and ingredients for food, animal feed and health products — modest growth, up 1% on a comparable currency-neutral basis.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Creating new flavors, fragrances and bioscience ingredients.

opex.name: Selling & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company — the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Amortization of acquired intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Goodwill impairment
opex.note: Writing down the recorded value of a past acquisition that is now worth less.

opex.name: Restructuring & other charges
opex.note: Restructuring charges of $5M plus $2M of losses on asset sales.

otherDetail: A $236M loss writing down the Food Ingredients business to its sale value, plus $46M of interest and $14M of other costs, partly offset by $2M of gains on business disposals.

takeaways.title: All three divisions grew
takeaways.text: Taste ($687M), Scent ($689M) and Health & Biosciences ($566M) all grew sales, with currency-neutral comparable growth of 5% overall.

takeaways.title: The loss is a write-down, not trading
takeaways.text: Operations earned $160M. The $127M continuing loss came from marking the soon-to-be-sold Food Ingredients business down by $236M, plus a $23M goodwill impairment.

takeaways.title: Guidance nudged up
takeaways.text: IFF raised the low end of its full-year sales outlook to $7.5–7.6B and completed a $500M share buyback in the quarter.

oneTimers: A $236M loss on assets classified as held for sale — writing the Food Ingredients disposal group down to what IFF expects to get for it; the sale is on track to close by the end of Q2 2027.
A $23M goodwill impairment inside operating costs.

The discontinued businesses being sold (Food Ingredients and SCL) actually made $72M this quarter, so IFF's total net loss was $55M (EPS -$0.22) rather than the $127M continuing loss shown in the chart.
footerNote: This page follows IFF's own presentation: continuing operations only. The Food Ingredients and SCL businesses being sold are reported as discontinued operations and are covered in the one-time items box.
